title: OR-04 · Distribution shift monitoring
summary: Monitor changes between represented cohorts under compatible spaces and a declared monitoring policy.

goals.title: Define the operation contract
goals.description: Define reference and current cohorts, windows, statistic, calibration, alert meaning and representation-version compatibility.

milestones.title: Specify inputs, outputs and requirements
milestones.description: Define reference and current cohorts, windows, statistic, calibration, alert meaning and representation-version compatibility. Create the Operation Contract and linked Requirements-and-Evidence Record before an experiment is admitted. Apply the linked shared admission, compatibility, temporal and evidence rules; the acceptance criteria below define this milestone’s completion boundary.
acceptance: The versioned Operation Contract and linked Requirements-and-Evidence Record specify input/output roles, claim scope, operation parameters, and typed failure or abstention conditions; existing charter links are design references, not evidence that this milestone is complete.

The contract inherits foundations-record-validation, foundations-temporal-integrity, foundations-data-protocol and foundations-lifecycle-admission. Any not-applicable rule is justified; a reusable interface can be drafted before instance selection, but an admitted run binds every required dataset, provider, artifact and protocol dependency.

Define repeated-monitoring cadence, reference update policy and sequence-level alert/error budget. Separate represented-population shift from provider/encoder changes and from changes in the relationship between representations and outcomes.

goals.title: Provide a reference implementation
goals.description: Provide a monitor that preserves cohort provenance and separates encoder changes from population changes.

milestones.title: Implement the agreed operation interface
milestones.description: Provide a monitor that preserves cohort provenance and separates encoder changes from population changes. The method, dataset and implementation slice remain to be selected. Apply the linked shared admission, compatibility, temporal and evidence rules; the acceptance criteria below define this milestone’s completion boundary.
acceptance: Conformance tests exercise the declared role/SpaceRef relationship, applicable temporal checks, malformed or unsupported inputs, stale fitted artifacts and explicit failure propagation; no rejected record becomes an ordinary vector or unreported omission.

Outputs retain parent/source lineage, representation kind, OperationRun identity, code/configuration and fitted-artifact identities. Engineering fixtures are labeled engineering-only and do not establish operation quality.

An incompatible or unverified provider/SpaceRef change emits a compatibility diagnostic rather than an ordinary population-drift score. Reference updates are versioned and cannot absorb assessment observations outside the admitted policy.

goals.title: Establish operation-specific evidence
goals.description: Test known and controlled changes with false-alert and detection-delay controls; distinguish measured shift from downstream harm.

milestones.title: Define and execute the admitted evaluation
milestones.description: Test known and controlled changes with false-alert and detection-delay controls; distinguish measured shift from downstream harm. Freeze the selected protocol, baselines and failure criteria before held-out assessment; retain negative outcomes and limitations. Apply the linked shared admission, compatibility, temporal and evidence rules; the acceptance criteria below define this milestone’s completion boundary.
acceptance: The admitted protocol fixes data partitions, instance and artifact identities, baselines, budgets, selection policy, metrics and failure criteria before held-out assessment. Diagnostic exposure, changes and repeated looks are indexed; a revised protocol does not silently reuse an exposed confirmation set.

Report the declared evaluation unit, uncertainty or its justified limitation, coverage including abstentions and failures, and relevant resource costs. Index every initiated run and its outcome under foundations-evidence-ledger; do not discard unsuccessful or inconclusive evidence.

A valid completed evaluation can be negative or inconclusive. Milestone completion is not a positive claim verdict, and invalid or unexecuted attempts alone cannot satisfy operation-quality evaluation acceptance.

Evaluate false-alert burden and detection delay across the declared monitoring sequence, including overlapping windows and reference updates; isolated pairwise tests do not substitute for the complete alert policy. Downstream harm remains a separately evaluated claim.
